note.question: Should a government or large buyer promise the R&D winner a follow-on production contract to elicit more private research effort at lower total procurement cost?
note.overview: Alongside a large empirical procurement study, the paper develops a substantive contest game: two R&D firms strategically choose costly research effort, the better prototype wins, and the government chooses whether to bundle that reward with a downstream production auction. Symmetric Nash effort and the government's optimal procurement payment are derived for firms with and without production capability.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: The government commits to an unbundled or bundled procurement regime and associated reward. In the research stage two firms simultaneously choose costly effort, prototype-quality shocks realize, and the higher-quality prototype wins. The winner develops the operational prototype under a cost-plus contract. In production, private costs realize; under unbundling the government runs a second-price auction, whereas under bundling the research winner receives the production contract and may produce or subcontract to the lowest-cost producer.
